title: Monthly Billing and Interest in Arrears on Rural Home Loans
content:
**Standard.** On Rural Home Loans, payments are due on the first day of each month and interest is paid in arrears: the payment due on the first of a month carries one month's interest for the preceding month on the 30-360 monthly convention, that is the principal balance after the previous payment's principal share times the note rate divided by 12, rounded to cents, booked as one interest bill with that due date. The monthly payment due is the monthly principal-and-interest payment plus the monthly escrow deposit; of the principal-and-interest part, the billed interest is the interest share and the rest the principal share. No payment is billed for a forborne month. The final payment is the billed interest plus all principal outstanding.

## The month's interest as a definition

One month's interest is the principal balance after the previous payment's principal share, multiplied by the note rate as a percentage, divided by 100 and divided by 12, rounded to cents; the number of days in the month plays no part. When a monthly payment is billed, the next due date moves to the first day of the following month.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

A loan with a principal balance of 180000.00 USD after the previous payment, a note rate of 6.125 percent, a monthly principal-and-interest payment of 1531.20 USD and a monthly escrow deposit of 410.00 USD:

| Item | Figure |
|---|---|
| Interest billed for the preceding month | 180000.00 multiplied by 6.125, divided by 100, divided by 12: 918.75 |
| Principal share | 1531.20 less 918.75: 612.45 |
| Monthly payment due | 1531.20 plus 410.00: 1941.20 |

If that payment were the final payment, it would instead be the billed interest of 918.75 plus all principal outstanding.
